STEPS:
1. Read the cases file; check schema "mako-cases-r87-v1", N = number of cases, 20 <= N <= 24; print cases_sha256 (sha256 of the file's bytes).
2. Extract the tool and the mutants from REV into DIR (scratch); print tool_sha256.

For each case, materialize home_files under DIR/home-<id>/ (create parent directories), then run the extracted tool as `python3 -I <tool> --config <home>/<config> --home <home> [--app-name X] [--urgency Y] [--mode M ...]` with TMPDIR=DIR and a 20 s timeout. Parse the stdout JSON. The case is correct iff every key in expect.effective equals the resolved value exactly, AND (refusals "none" means the refusals list is empty; "present" means it is non-empty), AND exit status is 0.
4. Two do-nothing controls, implemented INSIDE this counter (they never call the tool): `naive-toplevel` reads only the --config file's own key=value lines that sit before any [section] line and ignores include= and every section; `globals-include` follows include= (regular files under HOME, resolving ~ to home) and applies the global key=value lines of every file reached, ignoring every section. Each control scores its own correct count on the same cases with the same rule.
5. Mutants: for each mutant in the mutants file, copy the extracted tool to DIR, require that `old` occurs exactly once (else the mutant is a setup error: report it and count it as NOT killed), substitute, run the full case set, and mark the mutant killed iff at least one case verdict differs from the unmutated tool's verdict on that case.
6. Verdict: TARGET_MET iff tool_correct == N AND killed == M AND naive_correct < N AND globals_include_correct < N. Score = 10 * tool_correct / N, printed to 4 decimals.
7. Final stdout line exactly: `MADO_MAKO_CRITERIA: <TARGET_MET|TARGET_MISSED> rev=<REV> cases=<N> correct=<k> mutants=<M> killed=<j> naive_correct=<a> globals_include_correct=<b> score=<s> tool_sha256=<hex> cases_sha256=<hex>`. Exit 0 iff TARGET_MET, 1 for TARGET_MISSED, 2 for setup error (bad REV, unreadable cases, missing scratch root). The counter never writes outside DIR and never writes inside the repo.
8. --selftest: hermetic. Build a fixture repo with `D=$(mktemp -d) && git -C "$D" init -q`, verify toplevel equals D, write a tiny fixture tool and a 2-case fixture set, commit ONLY inside $D with an explicit `-c user.name=mado-selftest -c user.email=selftest@invalid`, then run the counter against it with REV pointing at that commit. Assertions must include: the scrubbed env works when GIT_DIR is set to a decoy; a deliberately wrong tool scores below N; a mutant with a non-unique `old` is a setup error and not killed; exit codes map as above. At least 8 assertions. Run `--selftest` ONCE with TMPDIR set to your scratch; keep the output and exit code in your report.
Do NOT run the counter against the lane's real REV; the L1 does that. Delete your scratch on exit.
